items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: Arthur Durbany, he used to play with me.

ctx.x: Is that the young Adolph Alexander or his father? No, no.

The young Alexander played with me once, you know, in my history. Yes. He played, coming playing saxophone, Tornet, and I was the one who got in to play saxophone. He started playing saxophone after he was with me. He didn't want to get on it. He didn't like it. The last step on behind him, he made good at it. He played saxophone. Arthur Durbany, he used to play with me.
The man in the band though, the Adolph Alexander, is that Tatt's father? That's right.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: That must have been the one I was trying to tell you about there, you see, that saxophone player that I had when they went out.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. And it's got you and then it's got Schatz. Willie Joseph, that's Kaiser. Emma is sitting at the piano. Arthur Durbany. And a saxophone player from St. Louis. It looks like he's playing a tenor or a C melody. I can't tell for sure. Must be a tenor. And then Robert Hall is another saxophone player. Willie Bontong playing the banjo and somebody...
That must have been the one I was trying to tell you about there, you see, that saxophone player that I had when they went out. What's his name?
